title: Selecting an adsorption medium for a defined PFAS water-treatment application
review_brief: Prepare a focused, data-grounded review explaining how an engineer should select an adsorption medium for a specified PFAS profile and water matrix.

components.requirement: Compare the adsorption mechanisms and material properties most relevant to PFAS chain length, functional group, and precursor composition.
Evaluate how dissolved organic matter, inorganic ions, pH, competing contaminants, and influent concentration alter performance.
Translate the evidence into conditional media-selection criteria rather than a universal material ranking.

data_extraction_objective: Extract adsorbent identity and properties, PFAS identity, water matrix, influent concentration, pH, co-constituents, dose or bed conditions, adsorption endpoint, quantitative result, and reported mechanism.

title: Translating PFAS adsorption results from batch tests to continuous treatment
review_brief: Prepare a focused review of when batch adsorption results do and do not predict column, pilot, or full-scale PFAS treatment performance.

components.requirement: Compare the information provided by equilibrium capacity, kinetics, fixed-bed breakthrough, bed volumes treated, and media lifetime.
Assess how flow, contact time, influent variability, competing constituents, and PFAS mixtures affect translation across scales.
Identify the minimum evidence needed to support a defensible service-life or scale-up claim.

data_extraction_objective: Extract study scale, adsorbent, PFAS and matrix, batch or flow configuration, contact time, flow and bed properties, capacity definition, breakthrough criterion, bed volumes, media lifetime, and uncertainty or scale-up limitation.

title: Deciding whether to regenerate or replace PFAS adsorption media
review_brief: Prepare a focused review of the evidence needed to choose among regeneration, replacement, and end-of-life management for PFAS-loaded adsorption media.

components.requirement: Compare regeneration approaches by PFAS release or destruction, recovered capacity, repeated-cycle performance, and material deterioration.
Account for liquid, gaseous, or solid residuals and distinguish transfer of PFAS from actual destruction.
Evaluate the operational, energy, chemical, cost, and sustainability evidence needed for a site-specific decision.

data_extraction_objective: Extract adsorbent and PFAS identity, loading protocol, regeneration or disposal method, operating conditions, desorption or destruction endpoint, capacity recovery, cycle number, material change, residual streams, energy, chemicals, and cost.

title: Selecting a membrane process for a defined PFAS feed water
review_brief: Prepare a focused, comparative review of how membrane processes should be selected for a specified PFAS composition, water matrix, and treatment objective.

components.requirement: Compare nanofiltration, reverse osmosis, adsorptive membranes, electrically assisted membranes, and relevant hybrid configurations by separation mechanism.
Evaluate effects of PFAS properties, membrane characteristics, pressure or flux, recovery, ions, organic matter, and fouling.
Define when reported rejection, adsorption, permeability, and energy results are sufficiently comparable to support process selection.

data_extraction_objective: Extract membrane type and properties, PFAS identity, feed matrix and concentration, pressure, flux, recovery, rejection or adsorption endpoint, fouling, permeability, energy, scale, and comparison limitations.

title: Managing PFAS residuals from membrane treatment
review_brief: Prepare a focused review of how membrane-derived PFAS concentrates and spent membrane materials should be characterized and managed within a treatment train.

components.requirement: Determine how recovery, concentration factor, PFAS composition, and co-contaminants define the retained stream.
Compare downstream concentration, destruction, recycle, disposal, and hybrid-treatment options using compatible endpoints.
Assess how residual management changes the energy, cost, environmental burden, and practical value of membrane separation.

data_extraction_objective: Extract membrane process, feed and retained-stream composition, recovery, concentration factor, residual volume, co-contaminants, downstream treatment, destruction or disposal endpoint, energy, cost, and scale.

title: Identifying the operating conditions that control PFAS foam fractionation
review_brief: Prepare a focused review of how PFAS properties, water chemistry, and reactor operation control foam-fractionation performance.

components.requirement: Evaluate effects of PFAS chain length and functional group, co-surfactants, organic matter, salts, and competing constituents.
Compare gas flow, bubble size, residence time, recycle, foam collection, and reactor configuration.
Interpret removal, recovery, enrichment, mass balance, and volume reduction as distinct performance measures.

data_extraction_objective: Extract PFAS and matrix composition, co-surfactants, reactor geometry, gas and flow conditions, bubble size, residence time, recycle, feed and foamate volumes, removal, recovery, enrichment, and mass-balance data.

title: Placing foam fractionation within a PFAS treatment train
review_brief: Prepare a focused review of when foam fractionation is useful as a concentration step and how the resulting PFAS-rich foamate should be managed.

components.requirement: Compare evidence from laboratory, pilot, and commercial applications for different feed waters and PFAS profiles.
Assess short-chain PFAS recovery, achievable volume reduction, stability of operation, and energy demand.
Evaluate downstream treatment or disposal of foamate and identify conditions under which the overall treatment train is advantageous.

data_extraction_objective: Extract feed source, PFAS profile, scale, operating duration, feed and foamate volume, recovery, enrichment, short-chain performance, energy, operational stability, downstream foamate treatment, and residual endpoint.

title: Matching a destructive technology to a PFAS-rich liquid stream
review_brief: Prepare a focused review of how electrochemical oxidation, non-thermal plasma, and sonolysis should be matched to a defined PFAS-rich liquid stream.

components.requirement: Compare the reaction environments, feed requirements, and PFAS structures for which each technology has been evaluated.
Assess effects of concentration, salinity, co-contaminants, reactor operation, kinetics, and energy demand.
Translate laboratory, pilot, and field evidence into conditional technology-selection criteria.

data_extraction_objective: Extract technology and reactor, feed matrix and PFAS loading, salinity and co-contaminants, operating conditions, kinetic basis, endpoint, energy metric, duration, scale, and stated implementation limitation.

title: Determining whether a PFAS destructive treatment achieved meaningful destruction
review_brief: Prepare a focused review of the measurements needed to distinguish disappearance of a target PFAS from transformation, defluorination, and broader destruction.

components.requirement: Compare parent-compound loss, transformation-product analysis, fluoride release, fluorine mass balance, and mineralization-related endpoints.
Evaluate how analytical scope, sampling time, detection limits, and unidentified products affect interpretation.
Define a defensible evidence hierarchy for reporting destruction while preserving technology, matrix, and scale limitations.

data_extraction_objective: Extract treatment and conditions, parent PFAS measurement, transformation-product scope, fluoride or fluorine measurement, mass-balance method, mineralization-related endpoint, detection limits, sampling time, unidentified fraction, and authors' endpoint terminology.

title: Designing PFAS treatment studies that remain valid in real water
review_brief: Prepare a focused review of how water-matrix effects should be tested and reported so that PFAS treatment performance can be translated beyond clean laboratory water.

components.requirement: Compare how organic matter, surfactants, inorganic ions, and other co-solutes alter physical separation and degradation processes.
Distinguish inhibitory, promotive, neutral, and interactive effects and relate them to treatment mechanism and PFAS properties.
Recommend a minimum matrix-characterization and matched-control framework for defensible cross-study comparison.

data_extraction_objective: Extract matrix constituent and concentration, PFAS identity, treatment, clean-water control, matrix-modified condition, direction and magnitude of effect, endpoint, proposed mechanism, constituent interaction, matched operating conditions, and study scale.
